title: Can money make you happy
paragraphs: What would make you happy? Really happy? A nice holiday, lazing on a tropical beach? Maybe a blowout meal with friends at a swanky restaurant? Or possibly splashing out on a pair of the latest designer jeans? All these pleasures cost money so does that mean we need lots of cash to feel good or does the old saying 'money can't buy happiness' still ring true?

This well-worn adage has been put to the test by scientists in Canada. They found that when used in the right way, money can bring us happiness. They discovered that when you use money to free up time, by paying someone to do your chores for example, you are happier. In an experiment, individuals reported greater higher life satisfaction if they used $40 to save time rather than spend it on material goods such as a new pair of shoes. But surprisingly, the researchers found that fewer than a third of individuals spent money to buy themselves time each month.

In our hectic lives time is one thing we seem to be short of. People are reporting a 'time famine', where they get stressed over the daily demands on their time. Psychologists say stress over lack of time causes lower well-being and contributes to anxiety and insomnia. But in many countries now, as incomes are rising, there is an option to buy more time.

This can be through hiring a cleaner to clean your house or outsourcing your ironing to someone else – giving us valuable extra hours to do the things we want to do. And in many forward-thinking companies, staff are given the opportunity to buy more time off or work flexibly.

Professor Dunn, who worked with colleagues at Harvard Business School, Maastricht University and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, says that "money can in fact buy time. And it buys time pretty effectively... and so my take home message is, 'think about it, is there something you hate doing that fills you with dread and could you pay somebody else to do that for you?' If so, then science says that's a pretty good use of money."

I would agree that buying more time makes me feel happier and more relaxed. But making time a priority over making money does come at a price; you have less cash to spend on the things you now have time to do. However there's another old saying that 'life is short and time is swift' so there's no time to waste and there's more to life than doing tedious housework!

vocabulary.entry: blowout [n.] /ˈbləʊaʊt/ 盛宴；狂欢 (口语)

vocabulary.translation: 我们举办了一场盛大的派对来庆祝他的生日。

vocabulary.entry: swanky [adj.] /ˈswæŋki/ 豪华的；时髦的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: They went to a swanky restaurant for their anniversary.
vocabulary.translation: 他们去了一家豪华的餐厅庆祝周年纪念日。

vocabulary.entry: ring true [phr.] /rɪŋ truː/ 听起来是真的；符合事实
vocabulary.example: His explanation doesn‘t ring true to me.
vocabulary.translation: 他的解释对我来说听起来不真实。

vocabulary.entry: chores [n. pl.] /tʃɔːz/ 家务；日常事务 (口语；单数: chore)
vocabulary.example: I need to finish my chores before I can go out.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要先做完家务才能出去。

vocabulary.entry: hectic [adj.] /ˈhektɪk/ 忙碌的；繁忙的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She has a hectic schedule this week.
vocabulary.translation: 她这周的日程安排很忙碌。

vocabulary.entry: famine [n.] /ˈfæmɪn/ 饥荒；缺乏 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The region is suffering from a severe water famine.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区正遭受严重的水资源匮乏。

vocabulary.entry: outsourcing [n.] /ˈaʊtsɔːsɪŋ/ 外包 (商业术语)
vocabulary.example: Outsourcing manufacturing to other countries can reduce costs.
vocabulary.translation: 将制造业外包给其他国家可以降低成本。

vocabulary.entry: flexibly [adv.] /ˈfleksəbli/ 灵活地
vocabulary.example: Employees can work flexibly to balance work and family.
vocabulary.translation: 员工可以灵活工作以平衡工作和家庭。

vocabulary.entry: tedious [adj.] /ˈtiːdiəs/ 乏味的；单调的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Data entry is a tedious job.
vocabulary.translation: 数据录入是一项乏味的工作。

vocabulary.entry: laze on [phr.] /leɪz ɒn/ 在……上悠闲地躺着 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I spent the afternoon lazing on the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 我整个下午都在海滩上悠闲地躺着。

vocabulary.entry: put to the test [phr.] /pʊt tə ðə test/ 对……进行考验；测试
vocabulary.example: The new software was put to the test by a group of experts.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新软件接受了一组专家的测试。

vocabulary.entry: free up [phr.] /friː ʌp/ 腾出；空出
vocabulary.example: Hiring an assistant freed up time for me to focus on other tasks.
vocabulary.translation: 雇佣助理腾出了时间让我专注于其他任务。

vocabulary.entry: be short of [phr.] /biː ʃɔːt əv/ 缺少；缺乏
vocabulary.example: We are short of staff this week.
vocabulary.translation: 我们这周人手短缺。

vocabulary.entry: contribute to [phr.] /kənˈtrɪbjuːt tuː/ 导致；促成
vocabulary.example: Poor diet contributes to many health problems.
vocabulary.translation: 不良饮食导致许多健康问题。

vocabulary.example: The take home message from the lecture is that exercise is essential.
vocabulary.translation: 讲座的关键信息是锻炼至关重要。

vocabulary.translation: 你应该把健康放在优先位置。

sentences.chinese: 或者可能是挥霍一笔钱买一双最新的名牌牛仔裤？

sentences.chinese: 他们发现，当你用金钱来腾出时间时，比如付钱让别人帮你做家务，你会更快乐。

sentences.chinese: 人们称这是“时间饥荒”，他们会因为日常对时间的需求而感到压力。

sentences.chinese: 心理学家说，对时间不足的压力会导致幸福感降低，并会引发焦虑和失眠。

sentences.english: And in many forward-thinking companies, staff are given the opportunity to buy more time off or work flexibly.
sentences.chinese: 而且在许多有前瞻性思维的公司里，员工有机会购买更多的休假时间或者灵活工作。

sentences.english: And it buys time pretty effectively... and so my take home message is, 'think about it, is there something you hate doing that fills you with dread and could you pay somebody else to do that for you?' If so, then science says that's a pretty good use of money."
sentences.chinese: 而且它相当有效地买到了时间......所以我的关键信息是，‘想一想，有没有什么你讨厌做的、让你充满恐惧的事情，你能不能付钱让别人来为你做呢？’如果有，那么从科学角度来说，这是对金钱的合理利用。”

sentences.english: I would agree that buying more time makes me feel happier and more relaxed.
sentences.chinese: 我同意购买更多的时间会让我感觉更快乐、更放松。

sentences.chinese: 但是把争取时间放在比赚钱更优先的位置确实是有代价的；在现在有时间做的事情上面，你可以花的钱会更少。

sentences.english: However there's another old saying that 'life is short and time is swift' so there's no time to waste and there's more to life than doing tedious housework!
sentences.chinese: 然而，还有另一句古老的谚语说“人生苦短，时光飞逝”，所以没有时间可以浪费，而且生活中还有比做乏味的家务更多的事情要做！
